title: Resilient CUDA-graph capture and strided replay for concurrent decode streams
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Intermittent mismatches and non‑replayable failures have been observed when using CUDA Graph capture across multiple concurrent decode streams. Root causes vary: allocator/address layout differences across captures, kernel selection heuristics that depend on ephemeral workspace sizes, and subtle timing differences when prefill work overlaps decode streams. This ticket designs and implements a capture-and-replay approach that makes kernel selection canonical at capture time, stabilizes memory/layout choices, and provides a robust verification and graceful-fallback strategy so multi-stream decode workloads do not regress correctness or latency SLOs.
acceptance_criteria: Replays succeed deterministically across 1000 synthetic multi-stream scenarios with varying batch/seq lengths
No functional regressions (token-level equivalence) for known customer workloads compared to pre-change baseline
End-to-end latency impact <= 5% on tail latency (p99) for typical decode traffic in staged tests
Feature gated and rolled out with monitoring and automatic rollback on replay mismatch alerts
tasks: Implement a capture-stable memory arena: dedicate a deterministic allocator for graph capture to produce stable device pointer layouts
Record canonical kernel choices in graph metadata at capture time and use these choices during replay to avoid heuristics divergence
Add a lightweight checksum validation step post-replay to detect divergence and trigger fallback to interpreter/JIT path
Introduce a per-model capture versioning header so replays can be rejected when model/quantization/config changes
Extend prefill scheduling to serialize capture-critical work when inter-stream address aliasing risk is high
Build a fuzz harness that generates interleavings of prefill/decode streams and fails on deterministic mismatches
Create CI e2e tests that run on representative GPU types (A100, H100) for both 16-bit/8-bit quantized paths
Document configuration flags and add console metric hooks for captures, replay success rate, and fallback counts
decisions: Use a dedicated capture allocator rather than trying to make the global allocator deterministic (simpler and lower risk)
Persist kernel-choice table with minimal metadata (kernel id + workspace size) inside the graph blob to prevent post-capture heuristic flips
Fallback strategy: prefer graph replay, on mismatch fall back to existing runtime path and emit an alert; do not auto-recapture in production during rollout
tradeoffs: Capture allocator increases peak memory usage by ~5-8% for models with large KV caches
Persisting kernel choices increases graph blob size slightly and couples capture to kernel ABI/version
Serializing some capture-critical prefill work may slightly increase capture latency but prevents hard-to-debug nondeterminism
testing_plan: Fuzz harness: 100k randomized interleavings including varying seq lengths, batch sizes, and attention patterns
Determinism suite: compare decoded token sequences across 10 identical replays after warm/cold allocations
Performance suite: run representative customer traces to measure p50/p95/p99 before and after with instrumentation
GPU matrix: validate on A100 (40/80GB), H100, and a smaller Ampere instance to surface allocator edge cases
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime flag: runtime.cudagraphs.resilient_replay = false by default
Stage 1: enable for internal QA workloads only (canary cluster) and run full fuzz harness
Stage 2: 1% customer traffic for non-critical models; monitor replay_success_rate, fallback_count, latency deltas
Stage 3: 10% traffic with increased observability and on-call ready
Stage 4: 100% after 72h healthy metrics and zero critical fallbacks; if any replay mismatch rate > 0.1% over 1h, auto-disable and rollback
